One-Mindfully is the second HOW skill: do one thing at a time and return attention to what is happening now.

## One thing at a time {#one-mindfully}

Thoughts about the past or future can still be present. The practice is not to erase them, but to avoid turning every thought into the current task. When planning, plan. When listening, listen. When washing one dish, wash that dish.

Attention will wander. Notice where it went and return without framing ordinary distraction as failure. Simplifying the task or reducing interruptions can help, but the essential skill is the return.

## Ordinary activities as practice {#ordinary-activities}

Choose one familiar activity:

- making tea or coffee;
- washing dishes or hands;
- cleaning one small area;
- showering or bathing;
- walking;
- having a conversation; or
- sitting for a brief meditation.

Notice the next concrete action and its sensory details. When the mind leaves, come back to this action in this moment.
